newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity trades lower under cash pressure.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity trades lower under cash pressure.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading lower Friday under pressure from cheaper Western power prices and perceptions of abundant electricity supplies particularily in the Pacific Northwest, industry sources said.
"There is a lot of power out there, the hydro(electric) levels are pretty well stocked and the cash came off yesterday," said one New York based futures trader.

As of 1200 EST, NYMEX February California Oregon Border (COB) power was trading down 75 cents at $13.90 following morning exchanges in a range of $13.75-14.00, while March COB was down 55 cents at a contract low of $11.80 per megawatt hour (MWh).
February Palo Verde (PV) was trading down 74 cents at $16.25 after trades as low as $16.00 per MWh, while March PV was offered at Thursday's settlement level of $14.50 per MWh.
The Bonneville Power Administration said it was offering peak power at $25.00-26.00 per MWh for Monday and Tuesday delivery. The agency did not offer peak, firm power for Friday delivery.

Expectations for hydroelectric generation levels were high, with the snowpack in California estimated to be well above normal. Water levels for hydrogeneration were also expected to be above normal in the Pacific Northwest this spring.
As of 1200 EST, NYMEX February Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading down 17.1 cents at $3.170 per million British thermal units.
"People are starting to realize that we are very well stocked energy-wise for the winter," the New York trader said, adding "soon will be trading March, and that is a swing month."
NYMEX said that as of 1135 EST an estimated total of four COB and 88 PV contracts had traded.
